language.script_notes: English with Māori place names, and many Scottish-derived place names in Otago and Southland (Dunedin, Invercargill) reflecting settlement history.

road_furniture.bollard_color: A bollard with a green stripe is common in southern Canterbury and pockets of eastern Southland.
road_furniture.curb_style: Long, quiet, single-lane bridges and gravel roads in remote areas.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: The whole island shares the 03 area code. Wooden utility poles appear in the snowy mountains and hollowed-out poles with sheep near them in the far south.

architecture.roof_style: Steeper roofs for snow and rain, in corrugated iron; Gothic Revival stone buildings with steep roofs in Christchurch and Dunedin.
architecture.roof_material: Corrugated iron, plus stone and slate on historic buildings.
architecture.wall_construction: Victorian and Edwardian stone and brick buildings in Dunedin and Oamaru (Oamaru has a Victorian-era white limestone precinct); simple huts and lodges in the mountains.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Cream limestone and grey stone in the historic towns, and muted weatherboard elsewhere.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Gothic Revival stone churches and university buildings; alpine lodges and ski villages around Queenstown and Wānaka; sheep station woolsheds; high-country farm huts.

nature.vegetation: Windbreak lines of pines and macrocarpa across the flat Canterbury Plains; tussock grassland and scrub in the high country; dense silver and mountain beech and podocarp rainforest (rimu, miro, Hall's tōtara) in Fiordland and on the west coast.
nature.terrain: A mountainous island backed by the Southern Alps, with braided rivers, glaciers and turquoise lakes; the vast, flat Canterbury Plains to the east; rolling farmland in Otago and Southland; deep glacier-carved fiords in the southwest.
nature.climate_signature: Cooler and drier in the east and wetter on the west coast and Fiordland; snowy peaks, big skies and sheep-covered high country.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Many campervans and tourist rentals around Queenstown and Milford Sound; 4WD utes on farms.

google_coverage.camera_generation: A mix of Gen 3 and Gen 4.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Good coverage of the main highways and towns, thinning in remote mountain and Fiordland areas; Stewart Island's dark-sand beaches are covered.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Highland-like mountains and lochs, Scottish place names and stone buildings in Dunedin
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The red bollard band wrapped fully around the post, red give-way text, corrugated-iron roofs, possum guards and Māori place names are not Scottish.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Glacier-carved fiords and beech-forest rainforest scenery in the southwest
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Left-hand traffic, English signage and the New-Zealand-style bollard settle it; Chile and Norway drive on the right.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same national road furniture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The South has the Southern Alps, the Canterbury Plains and fiords; the North has volcanoes, subtropical bush and rolling farmland.
